quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power can the front brake provide?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is true about a motorcycle horn?

options.text: It is useless.
Other people usually cannot hear it.
It can quickly get someone's attention.
It should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers may not notice it. Never depend only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, what should they do?

options.text: Pass in pairs.
Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.
Pass one at a time.
Avoid passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: When a group of motorcyclists passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. One rider must finish passing before the next rider starts.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be driving slowly while looking for a parking spot.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane, and pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver sees you.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist continuously scan the road ahead for?

options.text: Road conditions.
Traffic conditions.
Escape routes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead to watch for changing traffic, hazardous road conditions, and escape routes. Be ready to react to any changes.

questions.question: What should a face shield do?

options.text: Allow a clear view to both sides.
Prevent air from passing through it.
Be tight enough that glasses cannot fit underneath it.
Not fasten too tightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must have no scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: If you are riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
Always ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Do not worry about your position.
Always ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: When riding directly behind a car, ride in the center of your lane. This position is most likely to be visible in the car's rearview mirror, which drivers check more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax on the handlegrips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip both handlegrips firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding alongside another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit, then exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle may also block your escape route if a hazard appears. Either speed up or drop back.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. These signs tell riders the traffic rules. You must follow them.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to maintain your balance.
Maintain your speed to improve traction.
Not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and proceed as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and proceed as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid slippery roads. If you must ride on one, keep your motorcycle straight up. Go as slowly as you can.

questions.question: If you are riding in traffic when a small animal enters your lane, you should:

options.text: Do whatever you can, including swerving into other lanes, to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to try to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal. However, in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane to miss an animal can cause a crash with another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting a car.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never come into contact with the operator.
Sit as far back on their seat as possible.
Hold onto their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What may help if you experience slippage of your drive chain?

options.text: Tightening the chain
Loosening the chain
Using the throttle more
Applying the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Tightening the chain
questions.explanation: If your chain is slipping, try tightening it. If this does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Only take a few minutes.
Take more than an hour.
Be complicated to perform.
Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only take a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear wheel while braking on a good traction surface, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and down shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will still be under control if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should not rely on their mirrors to see what's going on around them because:

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than the mirrors on other vehicles, so you can't see as much.
Motorcycles, like cars, have blind spots.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road in front of you and they should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles, like cars, have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Turn your head to check your blind spots regularly.

questions.question: Which formation is best for keeping the riders in a group close together?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of your lane when it is wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is usually best, but this can change based on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way for a rider to increase visibility?

options.text: Wearing bright clothing with reflective material
Using a headlight at all times
Using turn signals
Waving at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To stay visible to other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake light properly. Waving does not increase visibility.

questions.question: Why is riding directly alongside another vehicle discouraged?

options.text: You may have difficulty getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may not see you and could swerve into your lane. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist discourage other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers who try to share your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may interfere with the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can make the motorcycle less stable and harder to balance.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Protects the eyes and face.
Is not recommended.
Is required by law.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects the eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough. While a motorcycle with a windshield does not legally require eye or face protection in all states, a face shield is still recommended.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Brake immediately.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift down to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars tightly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull to the side of the road safely. Do not use the brakes, as they can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you maintain?

options.text: At least four seconds behind the vehicle ahead.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.
You do not need to worry about following distance.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least four seconds behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds between themselves and the vehicle ahead. Keep an even larger distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: How much braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: Less than half of the motorcycle's braking power.
About 70 percent of the motorcycle's braking power.
It should only be used on wet roads.
It is the only brake you should use.

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent of the motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect riders?

options.text: They make you drowsy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make it hard to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, and anxiety cause drowsiness and can reduce your ability to ride safely. Before riding, learn how any medication you take affects your body.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required equipment on a legal motorcycle?

options.text: At least one headlight.
A brake light.
A windshield wiper.
A horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A windshield wiper.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must have a rearview mirror, horn, muffler, one or two headlights, a red brake light, and at least one brake. If the motorcycle has a passenger seat, it must also have footrests or floorboards for the passenger. A windshield wiper is not required.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, what should you do?

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Slowly zigzag across the grating.
Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Do not zigzag to compensate, as this is unsafe and forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: Which body part operates the gearshift lever?

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: How should you maintain control while turning?

options.text: Increase your speed before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright without leaning.
Look through the turn to plan your path.
Come to a complete stop before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look ahead through it by turning only your head. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: How should you make a quick stop?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a quick stop, apply both brakes together.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT reduce crash injuries?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Choose durable materials to protect yourself best.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you reduce crash risk?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Wear bright-colored clothing.
Do not ride during the day.
Find safer routes to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible to reduce crash risk. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake using the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake using the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and ride straight. Brake gently on the good tire only. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What should you do when making a regular stop?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow or stop. This habit makes it easier to use both brakes correctly in an emergency stop.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Lean with you during turns.
Hold onto the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you during turns.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control. They can hold onto handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: A friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use quiet roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride after drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Getting a group of friends involved to apply pressure is often effective.
